teams.heading: Fiji Latui collect four yellows and a red in Ireland XV rout
teams.body: Fiji's Latui side were reduced to 12 men for a spell on Friday as an Ireland XV ran in nine tries at Virgin Media Park in Cork. Tighthead Mesake Doge was binned for a high tackle on Ireland's Todd Lawlor. Within 30 seconds of his return he was shown a second yellow and a 20-minute red for collapsing a scrum. Isaia Lotawa's no-arms tackle cost a penalty try, and Apisalome Kuruisaqila was carded for a deliberate knock-on. Pita Lesivoukionoilau's interception and Jope Naseara's breakaway were Fiji's two tries.

lead.why: It is the only new Fiji event in the coverage; the Nicotera quotes have already run and the other items are Italy's or Ireland's stories.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje rejects win-at-all-costs mentality before England face the All Blacks
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje says his Christian faith sets limits on what he would do to win, and he named performance-enhancing drugs and betting on the game as examples. “Integrity is really important,” he said, in a week dominated by Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus's six-match ban for questioning whether officials were match-fixing. Itoje also called for referees to be respected. He wants Saturday's test against New Zealand at Twickenham to deliver back-to-back wins over the All Blacks for the first time since 2003.

lead.why: England's captain taking a personal moral stand before the All Blacks test is fresh England news, distinct from the Stuart and Borthwick stories already run.

teams.heading: France fitness coach Gaëtan Boissard tasked with keeping Bleus fresh for Argentina
teams.body: Today's test against Argentina comes a week after the 21-19 win over South Africa, and Rugbyrama casts recovery as a major issue for bodies put through the wringer. That job falls to France fitness coach Gaëtan Boissard. The Burgundian, whose father coached amateur sides, worked with France U20 when the 1999 generation won the Six Nations and the World Cup in France. The FFR then handed him a fitness contract in 2018.

lead.why: The referee row has already run, so this is the freshest France-specific piece, tied directly to today's Argentina test.

teams.heading: Ireland XV run in nine tries as Fijian Latui collect five cards
teams.body: The Ireland XV learned little from Friday's rout at Virgin Media Park, where the visitors were shown five cards in the first half and played with 12 men for a spell. Captain Gus McCarthy and Connacht's Daniel Ryan scored two tries each. Out-half Joey Carbery set up Ryan's opener and later dived under the posts after Fijian tighthead Mesake Doge was sent off for a second yellow. Paul Boyle withdrew late from the Ireland XV bench with a neck issue, and Scott Penny took his place.

lead.why: A fresh Ireland result from Friday night in Cork, and a different story from the Springbok team news already run.

teams.heading: Quesada hands Ortombina Italy's lineout calls and Miotti a debut against Fiji
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has made only two changes from the 14-19 defeat by Argentina in Genoa for Saturday's Nations Championship test v Fiji in Udine. Alessandro Ortombina starts at lock, with Federico Ruzza dropping to the bench. Quesada said Ortombina is at the right level to lead the lineout and brings physicality that can help against Fiji. Montpellier fly-half Domingo Miotti makes his Italy debut in place of Paolo Garbisi. The Italian federation's analysis notes Fiji had lineout-throwing problems in their 43-15 defeat by Ireland in Dublin.

lead.why: Fresh FIR selection analysis on Italy's two changes, led by the Ortombina lineout call. The captain's quotes and the Miotti back-story have already run.

teams.heading: Scotland U20 edge Ireland 31-29 in Cork as Irish leveller drifts wide
teams.body: Scotland U20 spoiled Ireland's U20s opener at Musgrave Park on Friday. They conceded five tries to a home pack dominant at scrum and maul but won through more accurate goal-kicking. Ireland out-half Paul Neary's late conversion to tie the game drifted wide. Scotland centre Harry Soboil was sin-binned for repeated infringements in an error-strewn first half, but wing Rory Caldwell and locks James Dalrymple and Christian Lindsay all crossed as the visitors punished two Irish yellow cards.

lead.why: The Darge and McDowall captaincy story already ran today, so the U20s' last-gasp win in Cork is the freshest Scotland result.

teams.heading: Justin Tipuric visits Wales camp but cannot talk Tandy into playing
teams.body: Ospreys coach Justin Tipuric spent Wednesday with Wales at their Vale Resort training base, days after the 35-28 win over New Zealand. He told WalesOnline he had tried to persuade head coach Steve Tandy, his former Ospreys team-mate and coach, to play again. "I tried to get him to play, but he didn't fancy it," said the three-time Lions tourist. He recalled Tandy, then of Neath, tripping him before a ruck in one of his first games for Aberavon. Tandy, preparing for Australia, says Wales run an open environment for club coaches.

lead.why: A fresh Wales camp story with a quotable old-rivalry anecdote, while the Prem confidence piece has already run.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi accuses Montpellier of broken deal as Piccardo misses France test
teams.body: Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi says centre Justo Piccardo's absence from Saturday's test against France was forced rather than chosen. Speaking on Friday, he said Piccardo had played 11 straight weeks and showed a GPS drop-off against Italy that pointed to fatigue. He accused Montpellier director of rugby Bernard Laporte and manager Joan Caudullo of breaking their agreement. Laporte told Rugbyrama that the June deal held only if the club avoided injuries, and cited a back-line crisis including Dimitri Delibes and Auguste Cadot.

lead.why: A fresh row between Argentina's head coach and Montpellier explains why a key centre misses tonight's test.

teams.heading: Every Wallabies match at home World Cup to screen free on Nine
teams.body: Nine Entertainment will broadcast half of the 52 matches at next year's men's World Cup in Australia, including all of the Wallabies' games, free on its channels and the 9Now streaming service, Rugby World reports. The remaining games go to subscription service Stan Sport, which also carries captain Harry Wilson's side against Wales in Cardiff. In Britain, ITV's deal with World Rugby, announced in July, keeps all 52 games free-to-air for a 24-team tournament running from 1 October to 13 November 2027.

lead.why: The freshest Australia item that has not already run: confirmation that every Wallabies match at the home World Cup will be free to watch.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones makes nine changes and an all-new front row for Japan
teams.body: Sojiro Otsuka, Kenji Sato and Ryosuke Iwaihara form the new front row for Saturday's Nations Championship test against Scotland at Murrayfield, as Japan head coach Eddie Jones reshapes his side after the 78-15 defeat by England. Among the nine changes, Shinya Komura comes in at fly-half, with Charlie Lawrence and Jisu Lee a new centre pairing. Warner Dearns and Naoto Saito are co-captains. Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend makes 11 changes of his own, resting Finn Russell.

lead.why: Japan's numbered team for Scotland is the day's fresh selection event, and it differs from the Latu call-up and Riley stories already run.

teams.heading: Try-bonus win over England would send All Blacks straight into grand final
teams.body: Fresh from last Saturday's 35-28 defeat by Wales in Cardiff, New Zealand know the arithmetic before Round 6 at Twickenham. The Guardian's Robert Kitson notes that a try-bonus victory over England books next Sunday's Nations Championship grand final regardless of South Africa's result against Ireland in Dublin. World Rugby rankings are also in play, according to Planet Rugby. Any win takes the All Blacks to No. 1 if the Springboks lose, while a heavy defeat could drop them to fifth, equalling their lowest ever position.

lead.why: It is the freshest, most corroborated story with a direct New Zealand stake, while the Kirk story has already run.

teams.heading: Franco Mostert replaces injured Ruan Nortje in Springbok second row v Ireland
teams.body: SA Rugby confirmed on Friday that Nortje, named at lock alongside Eben Etzebeth when the team was announced on Monday, picked up a niggle in training during the week. According to the union's statement, banned Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus opted for a cautious approach on Friday morning to give Nortje more time to recover. Mostert, a replacement against France and Italy, will earn his 88th cap when he takes the field in Dublin, while Lood de Jager stays on the bench as back-up lock.

lead.why: A late injury change to South Africa's starting XV is fresh hard news, and the Stick and Erasmus stories have already run.
